source.notes: Authenticated Guix pull/channel introduction was recorded for this pinned Free channel. This profile has not been evaluated or built on the channel; the lock is not package or firmware evidence.

kernel.notes: Pinned Guix commit 4e5195be (2026-11-25) selects linux-libre 7.3.5 by default and provides gnu/packages/aux-files/linux-libre/7.3-x86_64.conf. That config enables i915, nouveau, alx, snd_hda_intel/Realtek codec, SATA_AHCI, NVMe and xHCI. This is package-source/config evidence only; kernel build, package closure, initrd inclusion, runtime binding and physical function remain unassessed. The separate systems/wsm-gp107.modconfig belongs only to the proprietary NVIDIA Compatibility ISO and intentionally disables nouveau/i915; it must not be reused for this Free profile, which uses the stock linux-libre config.

notes: Board model and BIOS F22e are Windows-observed. Secure Boot state remains unknown.
No chipset or board driver requirement is inferred from the model name.
The pinned Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config has CONFIG_USB_XHCI_HCD=y and CONFIG_USB_XHCI_PCI=y; this is config evidence only, not physical USB controller or peripheral validation.

Intel PCH xHCI PCI host path does not request external firmware; a separate Renesas xHCI controller driver has a firmware loader, but that path is not the Intel H170 PCH controller. No physical USB enumeration has been performed.

evidence.source: Pinned Guix Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 kernel config
evidence.summary: The pinned default config sets CONFIG_INTEL_MEI=m and CONFIG_INTEL_MEI_ME=m. This establishes module availability in the source config, not package/initrd inclusion or runtime binding.

evidence.source: wsm-os HECI hardware trace and CSME architecture
evidence.summary: The observed HECI PCI function is 8086:a13a. ME firmware 11.8.50.3425 is a separate pre-OS BIOS/CSME firmware domain; the Linux MEI host interface does not load that firmware as a Guix host package.

evidence.source: wsm-os HECI hardware trace (bare-metal Kali Linux)
evidence.summary: On physical Skylake/i5-6400 hardware, /dev/mei0 exchanged MKHI firmware-version and capability requests/responses; PCI ID 8086:a13a and ME firmware 11.8.50.3425 were observed. This proves the basic HECI path on the prior Kali Linux environment, not WSM Guix runtime binding or every MEI client feature.

notes: Owner-specific bare-metal Kali Linux trace observed PCI ID 8086:a13a and successful basic MKHI request/response through /dev/mei0; BDF is not recorded.
The host-side mei_me driver is separate from Intel CSME firmware 11.8.50.3425, which remains in the motherboard BIOS/SPI domain.
This physical test does not prove runtime binding in the WSM Guix profile or all MEI client functions.

identity_evidence.summary: Owner-specific read-only hardware trace observed HECI PCI ID 8086:a13a; BDF not recorded.

evidence.source: wsm-os BIOS F22e FIT and physical microcode evidence
evidence.summary: For exact CPUID 0x000506E3 (i5-6400), BIOS F22e contains microcode revision 0xC2 dated 2017-11-16; the UEFI pre-OS probe observed 0xC2, while the Windows host later reported 0xD6 dated 2019-10-03. Without an OS early-update package, Linux can still boot using BIOS-provided 0xC2; this evidence does not assert the latest available Intel revision.

evidence.source: Linux x86 microcode loader documentation
evidence.summary: The Linux kernel can apply Intel microcode early from the initrd at kernel/x86/microcode/GenuineIntel.bin. This is an OS firmware package path separate from the BIOS-provided microcode; early loading is distinct from the unsafe/disabled-by-default late-load path.

evidence.source: Intel official Linux processor microcode repository license
evidence.summary: Intel's official microcode package license permits binary redistribution without modification and prohibits reverse engineering, decompilation and disassembly. The update package is nonfree; it must not enter the WSM Free closure.

notes: CPU identification is Windows-observed. This profile makes no claim about microcode package inclusion.

BIOS F22e already loads microcode 0xC2 for this exact CPU before the OS; Windows later applies 0xD6. A Linux-libre Free profile without Intel's nonfree early-update package can boot on BIOS microcode 0xC2, but does not reproduce the observed Windows 0xD6 update. Keep microcode revision in benchmark metadata; do not late-load or reverse engineer the blob.
The pinned Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config has CONFIG_MICROCODE=y and disables late loading; the early Intel update package remains optional/nonfree and is not included in the Free closure.

evidence.source: Pinned Guix Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 default kernel configuration
evidence.summary: The default Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config at pinned Guix commit 4e5195be sets CONFIG_DRM_I915=m. This establishes that the driver is configured as a built-in or module in the source config; it does not prove a built kernel, package/initrd inclusion, runtime binding, or physical function.

evidence.source: Linux i915 Skylake DMC firmware path
evidence.summary: The Skylake i915 driver loads DMC firmware; if it is unavailable, upstream logs that runtime power management is disabled. This makes DMC optional for basic graphics but required for the full DMC-backed runtime power-management path. This evidence does not prove the firmware is present in Guix, H170 runtime binding, or physical display/graphics validation.

evidence.source: Linux-firmware Skylake i915 firmware inventory and Intel license
evidence.summary: WHENCE lists Skylake DMC and GuC firmware under LICENSE.i915. The vendor license permits binary redistribution only without modification and prohibits reverse engineering/decompilation/disassembly. This is nonfree firmware; it must not enter the WSM Free closure. GuC/HuC features require separate workload-specific assessment.

notes: Candidate free graphics path only. DRM/KMS, firmware needs, Guix package closure and Plasma session have not been tested on this target.

Skylake i915 DMC firmware is used for display runtime power management; without it upstream disables runtime PM, while basic graphics is a separate path. GuC is optional for base driver operation and HuC/media features are workload-specific. DMC/GuC firmware is distributed under Intel's nonfree LICENSE.i915, not part of the WSM Free closure.

driver_candidates.name: Nouveau + Mesa/NVK (upstream lists Kepler and later; H170 validation pending)
userspace_candidates: NVK (upstream generation range includes Kepler/Pascal; exact 10de:1c82 runtime not assessed)

evidence.source: Mesa NVK driver documentation
evidence.summary: Current upstream documentation lists Kepler and later GPU generations for NVK, Vulkan 1.4 conformance for officially supported GPUs, and Linux kernel >=6.6. A developer-only override may enumerate poorly tested or broken GPUs. This is generation-level upstream evidence only; exact 10de:1c82 enumeration, Guix package closure, firmware, binding and functional validation remain unassessed.

evidence.source: Nouveau upstream feature matrix
evidence.summary: Nouveau upstream lists Vulkan support from Kepler onward, but notes that GP10x Pascal has no practical reclocking path because the required firmware access is signature-restricted. This is a generation-level performance limitation; it does not establish exact GP107 runtime binding, firmware presence, package closure, or H170 functional validation.

evidence.source: Pinned GNU Guix Mesa/Linux-libre package definitions
evidence.summary: At pinned Guix channel commit 4e5195be (2026-11-25), Mesa 26.2.6 explicitly enables the nouveau Vulkan driver on x86_64 with -Dvulkan-drivers=amd,intel,intel_hasvk,nouveau,swrast,virtio and includes Mesa Cargo inputs. The default linux-libre alias is 7.3.5, above NVK's Linux 6.6 minimum. This proves package configuration intent only, not a successful Guix build, ICD installation, runtime binding, firmware load, or GP107 functional test.

evidence.source: Pinned Guix Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 default kernel configuration
evidence.summary: The default Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config at pinned Guix commit 4e5195be sets CONFIG_DRM_NOUVEAU=m. This establishes that the driver is configured as a built-in or module in the source config; it does not prove a built kernel, package/initrd inclusion, runtime binding, or physical function.

evidence.source: gp107-nvidia-re physical Nouveau/NVK boot and vector-add witness
evidence.summary: On the external GP107 research test host, PCI 10de:1c82 at 0000:01:00.0 bound to nouveau under Kali Linux 7.2.15+kali-amd64; NVK driverID=24, Mesa 26.1.6-1, Vulkan API 1.3.354. A clean-room 1024-element vector-add dispatch completed, fence signaled, host readback checksum matched (0xa52ce165), and a no-op negative control failed as expected. This proves Nouveau binding and one NVK compute workload for a GP107/GTX 1050 Ti on that external test host. Its motherboard/CPU/BIOS are not proven to match the H170 reference machine. Exact GP107 GR firmware package/blob provenance was not captured; kernel log says PMU firmware unavailable (a separate path). This is not validation of the WSM Guix Free profile or H170 runtime.

notes: Windows nvidia-smi reported physical adapter location 00000000:01:00.0. That BDF is not a PCI vendor:device ID.
Do not infer reclocking, full acceleration, firmware presence or usable KDE acceleration from detection. Pascal performance limitations must be documented.

Mesa's current NVK documentation lists Kepler and later GPUs, states a Linux 6.6 minimum, and documents a developer-only override that can expose poorly tested or broken GPUs. This upstream scope does not prove enumeration or functional support for PCI ID 10de:1c82.

evidence.source: Linux Nouveau GP107 GR implementation and ACR fallback
evidence.summary: Upstream GP107 GR declares FECS/GPCCS firmware and GR software-context blobs. Its firmware interface selects gm200_gr_load with ACR handlers for FECS and GPCCS; the no-firmware fallback returns -ENODEV. These blobs are required for Nouveau GP107 GR 3D/compute initialization. This does not establish basic KMS/display behavior without them, nor Guix package presence, redistribution rights, runtime binding, or H170 functional validation.

evidence.source: Linux-firmware WHENCE and NVIDIA firmware license
evidence.summary: The GP107 Nouveau firmware group is listed as redistributable under LICENCE.nvidia. This is a vendor license, not an open-source license; it contains restrictions on reverse engineering and firmware translation. This evidence does not resolve jurisdiction-specific interoperability exceptions or establish package integration. The WSM Free profile must not ship these blobs.

notes: Windows nvidia-smi reported physical adapter location 00000000:01:00.0. That BDF is not a PCI vendor:device ID.
Do not infer reclocking, full acceleration, firmware presence or usable KDE acceleration from detection. Pascal performance limitations must be documented.

Separate GP107 research repository documents a physical NVK vector-add pass for PCI ID 10de:1c82 on its own test host. That host is not proven to be this H170 board; the result does not establish H170 runtime binding, display support, daily-driver stability, or this profile's functional_validation.

GP107 GR firmware dependency is now source-confirmed for 3D/compute: Nouveau declares FECS/GPCCS firmware and its no-firmware fallback returns -ENODEV. Basic display/KMS without GR firmware remains a separate unassessed question.

External GP107 research-host evidence proves Nouveau binding and a clean-room NVK vector-add compute pass on a GTX 1050 Ti under Kali Linux 7.2.15/Mesa 26.1.6. The test host is not proven to be the H170 reference machine, and exact GR firmware package/blob provenance was not captured. This is not H170 or WSM Guix Free-profile validation; keep H170 runtime_binding unknown and functional_validation not-run.

Kernel version is part of the display result on this GPU: a NULL pointer dereference in drm_atomic_commit during GP107 initialization was reported on 2026-11-02 after commit 2652aca460dc (atomic modesetting by default for NV50+), worked around with nouveau.atomic=0, and fixed in mainline by ed7fb901fce3 (2026-11-25). A display failure in the regression window must not be read as a hardware fault. Source: juv4uk/gp107-nvidia-re docs/48.

The pinned kernel is inside that window: linux-libre 7.3.5 was released 2026-11-17 and the fix reached mainline 2026-11-25, so 7.3.5 predates it and carries the regression (7.3.6, 2026-11-23, does too). A display failure at boot on this profile is therefore expected rather than surprising; mitigate by pinning a kernel at or after the fix, or by booting with nouveau.atomic=0, or state the limitation in the release notes. Source: juv4uk/gp107-nvidia-re docs/48.

identity_evidence.source: Owner-shared Windows PowerShell Get-PnpDevice -Class Display inventory
identity_evidence.summary: VEN_10DE DEV_1C82 SUBSYS_33511462 REV_A1. The separately observed BDF 00000000:01:00.0 is a bus address, not a vendor:device identifier.

evidence.source: Linux alx PCI ID table and LKDDb
evidence.summary: The upstream alx PCI table includes ALX_DEV_ID_E2200; LKDDb maps the E2200 controller to PCI ID 1969:e091. The owner inventory names Killer E2200 but does not record its exact PCI ID, so the manifest pci_ids remains empty pending physical/Windows ID evidence.

evidence.source: Pinned Guix Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 default kernel configuration
evidence.summary: The default Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config at pinned Guix commit 4e5195be sets CONFIG_ALX=m. This establishes that the driver is configured as a built-in or module in the source config; it does not prove a built kernel, package/initrd inclusion, runtime binding, or physical function.

evidence.source: Linux alx driver source audit
evidence.summary: The seven-file upstream alx driver directory (Makefile, alx.h, ethtool.c, hw.c, hw.h, main.c, reg.h) contains no request_firmware or MODULE_FIRMWARE dependency. This means no host-loadable firmware is required by the alx driver; it does not prove physical binding or traffic functionality.

notes: Owner profile observes a Killer E2200 adapter. Exact PCI vendor:device ID, package availability, binding and DHCP/traffic test remain unknown.

The upstream alx source has no host-loadable firmware dependency. E2200 maps to 1969:e091 in LKDDb, but the exact PCI ID for this machine has not been observed; do not populate pci_ids or claim binding from the model name alone.

GIGABYTE board specifications differ by revision: Rev. 1.0 lists Killer E2201, Rev. 1.1 lists Killer E2400; Windows owner inventory reports the E2200 device label. Board revision and exact PCI ID are not recorded, so the E2200 label is not treated as a confirmed silicon revision.

evidence.source: Pinned Guix Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 default kernel configuration
evidence.summary: The default Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config at pinned Guix commit 4e5195be sets CONFIG_NVME_CORE=y and CONFIG_BLK_DEV_NVME=y. This establishes that the driver is configured as a built-in or module in the source config; it does not prove a built kernel, package/initrd inclusion, runtime binding, or physical function.

evidence.source: Linux NVMe host driver source
evidence.summary: The generic Linux NVMe host driver does not request a firmware blob to operate the controller. SSD-internal firmware is device-managed and is not a host-loadable Guix firmware dependency; this does not assess the SSD's own firmware version or update policy.

notes: Storage model/capacity are Windows-observed. No read/write validation or initrd requirement is claimed.
No host-loadable firmware is required by the generic NVMe host driver. The SSD's internal firmware is separate from the host driver and has not been inspected or updated.

No host-loadable firmware is required by the generic AHCI host driver. Firmware inside the SATA drives is separate and has not been inspected or updated.

evidence.source: Pinned Guix Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 default kernel configuration
evidence.summary: The default Linux-libre 7.3 x86_64 config at pinned Guix commit 4e5195be sets CONFIG_SND_HDA_INTEL=m and CONFIG_SND_HDA_CODEC_REALTEK=m. This establishes that the driver is configured as a built-in or module in the source config; it does not prove a built kernel, package/initrd inclusion, runtime binding, or physical function.

evidence.source: Linux HD-audio driver documentation
evidence.summary: The standard HDA codec path does not require a vendor firmware blob. An optional snd-hda-patch-loader feature can load a user-supplied pseudo-firmware initialization patch via request_firmware; that optional override is not a baseline hardware firmware dependency. The exact onboard codec ID remains unconfirmed.

notes: Windows lists audio endpoints. Codec-level enumeration, firmware, audio service setup and playback/capture remain untested.

Standard HDA/Realtek codec support has no required vendor firmware blob; an optional user-supplied HDA initialization patch is a separate override. Exact codec ID (including any ALC1150 claim), UCM configuration and playback/capture remain untested.
The same pinned kernel config enables CONFIG_SND_HDA_PATCH_LOADER=y; this enables the optional user-supplied patch mechanism, not a required vendor firmware blob.
GIGABYTE specifications for GA-H170-Gaming 3 Rev. 1.0 and Rev. 1.1 list Realtek ALC1150; this is board-vendor evidence, not physical codec enumeration. Keep exact codec ID unknown until observed.
Free baseline only; no Nonguix channel, proprietary NVIDIA package, substitute key or firmware bundle is added.
No driver candidate in this draft is asserted present, bound or functional.
The owner profile is Windows-observed; WSL2/QEMU inventory cannot prove physical Linux PCI binding.
